title: Finite reduction of reconstruction
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and let $A,I,P_n,(P_n)_T,A_T$ be the Noetherian coefficient datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\Proet},A_T))$ be derived $I$-complete, meaning that its Koszul completion map of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] is an isomorphism. Let $K_\bullet$ be its strict quotient tower, obtained from a functorial K-flat representative $QK$ by $QK\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T$, as in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Write $L=\Rlim K_\bullet$ for [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit]. In this statement $M\otimes_A^L P_a$ abbreviates $M\otimes_{A_T}^L(P_a)_T$; no identification of ordinary $D(A)$ with this sheaf derived category is intended.

For every $a\geq1$, evaluation $L\to K_a$, with $K_a$ regarded as an object over $(P_a)_T$, has adjoint the derived counit, and this is a functorial isomorphism
$$
L\otimes_{A_T}^L(P_a)_T\xrightarrow{\sim}K_a.
$$
Moreover $(-)\otimes_{A_T}^L(P_a)_T$ commutes with the two derived countable products in the Roos triangle of this strict tower, all products and tensors being computed in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\Proet},A_T))$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] to the datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. It identifies $A_T\otimes_{\underline A}^L\underline{P_a}$ with $(P_a)_T$. Choose a bounded finite-projective resolution $F_a^\bullet\to P_a$, which exists by the perfectness assumption. The same lemma gives a bounded representative $E_a^\bullet=A_T\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{F_a^\bullet}$ of $(P_a)_T$, with each term a direct summand of a finite sum of $A_T$. Thus the perfect complex used below is a complex of sheaves over $A_T$, not an ordinary $A$-module complex.

source.place: coefficient interpretation required for the bounded finite-projective representative

proof.text: By [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] the completion map $\eta:K\to L$ agrees with the strict quotient-tower completion map and is an isomorphism because $K$ is derived $I$-complete. For each $a$ its composite with the evaluation $p_a:L\to K_a$ is the canonical reduction map $u_a:K\to K_a$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. This uses the map compatibility in the reconstruction statement, not merely an abstract isomorphism between the objects.

source.place: proof, first sentence: Koszul completion and quotient-tower completion map

proof.text: Let $\epsilon_a:L\otimes_{A_T}^L(P_a)_T\to K_a$ be adjoint to $p_a$ under derived extension and restriction of scalars. The identity $p_a\eta=u_a$ from [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] implies that $\epsilon_a(\eta\otimes^L1)$ is adjoint to $u_a$. Since $K_a=K\otimes_{A_T}^L(P_a)_T$ by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], that adjoint is $1_{K_a}$. Tensoring the isomorphism $\eta$ with $(P_a)_T$ gives an isomorphism, so $\epsilon_a=(\eta\otimes^L1)^{-1}$. This identifies the specified counit, not just some isomorphism. The completion and reduction maps are functorial, so their inverses and this counit are functorial.

source.place: proof, finite-level identification, with completeness made explicit

proof.text: For the two products $R\!\prod_nK_n$ in [prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle], apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-tensor-products] with the representative $E_a^\bullet$ of step 1. It yields the canonical product comparison isomorphism for each occurrence. Naturality with respect to every transition $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ implies compatibility with the shift $s$, and hence with $1-s$: the $n$-th projection of either composite is the tensor of the transition composed with the $(n+1)$-st projection. Thus both product comparisons are precisely those attached to the Roos triangle; no assertion that the reduced tower is constant is used.

source.place: proof, last sentence: the two products of the Roos triangle

source_correction.reason: STATEMENT-DISPUTED in the unrestricted reading: the source omits K and derived completeness from the statement, although its source note expressly assumes a derived-complete K and its proof invokes its strict quotient tower. This repair restores those hypotheses and makes all tensors over A_T explicit.
source_correction.counterexample: A=Z, I=(2), K_1=F_2, K_n=0 for n>1, all transition maps zero: 1-s is the identity on the product F_2, so Rlim=0 but K_1 is nonzero. This is not the strict quotient tower of a derived-complete object.

blueprint_update.statement:
For every $a\geq1$, the derived counit from inverse limit to evaluation
induces a functorial isomorphism

$$
 (\Rlim K_\bullet)\otimes_A^LP_a\xrightarrow{\sim}K_a.
$$

Moreover, $(-)\otimes_A^LP_a$ commutes with the two derived countable
products occurring in the Roos triangle attached to the derived inverse-limit
construction.

proof.text:
By [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] the Koszul completion is identified
with $\Rlim K_\bullet$, so we verify the statement for the Koszul completion:
tensoring the strict Koszul tower with the bounded finite-projective
representative of $P_a$ and evaluating at the $a$-th stage gives the
canonical isomorphism. The commutation with the two derived products is the
compatibility of tensor with products in the Roos triangle of
[prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle].
